v1_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month to ~1,220/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05), coinciding with manual-read route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target for 9,200 accounts (E-01), which forces estimate-substitution billing responsible for the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (41% of 3,025 disputed bills, E-03). The remaining 59% of disputes are on ACTUAL reads whose cause is not yet established, and the surge is neither a response-speed problem (SLA compliant, E-04) nor tariff-driven (zero logged changes, E-02).
v2_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1,220/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05). Of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (41% of 3,025 total, E-03), 1,184 (95.5%) had a valid AMI read exported but were rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-10). This is explained by validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares the raw AMI register value against 12-month m3 history without unit scaling (E-11), while v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) record consumption in 0.1 m3 units (E-12) — causing legitimate v4.2 reads to be misread as anomalous highs and substituted with estimates, producing wrong bills that customers dispute. The cause of the remaining 59% of disputes (1,785 ACTUAL-read bills) is not yet established by current evidence.
